articles.title_zh: 黎巴嫩的艺术项目将美丽带入危机
articles.content: With Lebanon currently being impacted by war, a refugee crisis, and more, stories of beauty can be hard to come across. For ministries active in Lebanon, meeting the spiritual, physical and emotional needs of a country just trying to survive can take its toll. Horizons International’s Pierre Houssney said that despite the trauma the country faces due to the fallenness of man in a sinful world, God has still created a world that contains beauty. “And I think that beauty speaks to people’s hearts about God, especially when it’s not just beauty, you know, for beauty’s sake, but when it’s beauty in the name of Christ,” Houssney said. “In the midst of the trauma, in the midst of the poverty, we’re trying to give opportunities for believers, who have artistic gifts, to have a prophetic voice through their art to the society, so that we can be calling out for Christ in the midst of the crisis.” Some of these opportunities for creating beauty are fine art classes offered by Horizons International. Horizons International has had up to 35 students at one time participating in these classes revolving around painting or drawing. Students in visual arts classes had the opportunity to participate in an exhibition in Beirut called “His Touch.” People from the community were invited to see the work of beginner students as well as 10 different Christian artists. Graphic design classes offer a more practical element, allowing students to learn a skill they could use in their everyday lives. On the worship side of things, music theory and classes in instruments are helping raise up worship leaders for local churches. One unit teaching guitar, piano, and drums to beginners looking to lead worship at their church had 70 people participate. “And so this new generation needs training, and they need, you know, they need mentoring, and they need to have those skills so that they can, they can lead their congregations in worship,” Houssney said. Though some may have more trouble connecting visual arts directly with ministry, Houssney says social media helps make that connection more clear. Beautiful videos that contain scripture messages alongside visual art tend to get a higher viewership. When posts like that get more views, they can potentially bring more people to Christ. “And so it needs to be beautiful. It needs to be excellent, it needs to be well done. And that’s what our Lord deserves,” Houssney said. “That’s not just what social media deserves.” Currently, Horizons International has to spread resources between humanitarian aid like food and medicine and projects that glorify God through the arts. In the midst of the crisis in Lebanon, pray for God to provide the resources for canvases, studio spaces, art instructors and more. Houssney also says what an organization like Horizons International is here for is to see God open more and more hearts to the Gospel. “So I’m not praying that the church would have less hardship. I’m not praying for you know, for less, you know, political chaos. What I’m praying for is that, through it all, people would continue to open their hearts, and that God will be glorified.” Learn more about the work of Horizons International in Lebanon by visiting https://www.horizonsinternational.org/lebanon-crisis .
articles.content_zh: 黎巴嫩目前受到战争、难民危机等影响, 对活跃在黎巴嫩的各部来说,满足一个国家的精神、身体和情感需求,只是为了生存而努力,这可能会造成损失。 Horizons International的Pierre Houssney说,尽管由于人类在罪恶世界中的堕落,国家仍然面临创伤,但上帝仍然创造了一个包含美丽的世界。 “我认为,美丽对人们的心来说是关于上帝的,特别是当它不仅仅是为美丽着想,而是以基督为名的美丽时,”Houssney说。 “在创伤中,在贫困中,我们试图给那些拥有艺术天赋的信徒机会,通过他们的艺术向社会发出先知的声音,以便在危机中呼唤基督。” 其中一些创造美貌的机会是地平线国际提供的精美艺术课. 地平线国际曾经有多达35名学生参加这些围绕绘画或绘画而旋转的课. 视觉艺术课的学生有机会在贝鲁特参加一个名为“他的触摸”的展览。 社区人士被邀请观看初学者和10名不同的基督教艺术家的作品. 图形设计课程提供了更实用的元素,让学生学习在日常生活中可以使用的技能. 在事物的崇拜方面,乐器中的音乐理论和课程正在帮助培养地方教会的崇拜领袖. 一个教吉他,钢琴,和鼓的单位在他们的教堂里为初学者寻找引领崇拜,有70人参加. “因此,这新一代需要培训,他们需要,你知道,他们需要指导,他们需要这些技能,以便他们能够领导他们的教会进行礼拜。” 虽然有些人可能更难直接将视觉艺术与部委联系起来, 包含经文信息与视觉艺术的美丽视频往往获得更高的收视率. 当这样的帖子获得更多的观点时,它们有可能将更多的人带入基督. “因此,它必须是美丽的。 它需要出色,需要做得很好。 这才是我们的主应得的。 这不仅仅是社交媒体应得的。 目前,地平线国际必须在食品和医药等人道主义援助和通过艺术来赞美上帝的项目之间分配资源。 在黎巴嫩危机中,祈求上帝为画布、工作室空间、艺术教员等提供资源。 霍斯尼还说,像地平线国际这样的组织在这里是为了看到上帝对"福音"越来越开放的心. 我并不祈祷教会会减少困难。 我并不是为你们祈祷, 我所祈祷的是,通过这一切,人们将继续敞开心扉,而上帝将受到赞美。” 透过访问https://www.horisonsinternational.org/lebanon-crisis,

articles.title_zh: v.容忍
articles.content: This incident took place over 15 years ago, and yet, I remember it clearly.  In the buzz of daily life, it is easy to get caught up in the carelessness of the checklists, and forget the intentionality of abiding in Him. I remember how frantic I was once at or late deadline and how frustrated I was at all the problems we were having in getting the program together.  We’d all kinds of equipment failure throughout the day and I was going to have to drive the program across town to get it uploaded to the satellite.  It was already 7 pm and the babysitter was calling me every 10 minutes. Then, I got a call from a lady with a gentle Creole accent. She told me, “I felt led to call you and pray with you.”  I SO didn’t want to talk to this lady, wasn’t interested in being prayed over, and really just wanted to leave to get this program fed and pick my 2-year old up.  I was impatient when I responded to her.  Rather than take insult from what was probably a curt rebuff,  she just said , “Wow. You REALLY need the peace of our heavenly Father on your heart right now.” And…she burst out in song.   Now I’m wondering why I’m on the phone with this crazy lady, and then she prayed through the worship song and then rolled right into praying for me, for my distress, for the things I thought I needed to do…and prayed that I would be still and listen, that my heart would be quiet long enough to remember the awe of God, and that the joy would come back to my heart as we produced MNN… The more she prayed, the more convicted I grew and I realized I was caught up in the ‘do’ and not the ‘be’…and THEN she pulled out the big guns: the story of Mary and Martha. Luke 10:38-42 New International Version (NIV) At the Home of Martha and Mary 38 As Jesus and his disciples were on their way, he came to a village where a woman named Martha opened her home to him. 39 She had a sister called Mary, who sat at the Lord’s feet listening to what he said. 40 But Martha was distracted by all the preparations that had to be made. She came to him and asked, “Lord, don’t you care that my sister has left me to do the work by myself? Tell her to help me!” 41 “Martha, Martha,” the Lord answered, “you are worried and upset about many things, 42 but few things are needed—or indeed only one. [ a ] Mary has chosen what is better, and it will not be taken away from her.” She ended our conversation with, “Sometimes, it’s ok to be Mary and sit at the feet of Jesus.  Stuff will still be there to do. It will eventually get done.  But the lasting investment is remembering to sit and BE at the feet of Jesus.” It was a much needed gentle rebuke along with a little encouragement from an unknown sister in Christ that I still remember to this day…thousands of productions later.   What we do is important…but not at the risk of forgetting to abide in Christ.

articles.title_zh: Koinonia
articles.content: Koinonia (Koy-no-nee’-ah) is a Greek word, occurring 20 times in the Bible, which means “fellowship” or “brotherly love.” It carries with it the meaning of a committed, trustworthy, and dependable relationship. Such a relationship can be experienced through participation, sharing, giving, and contributing. The first occurrence of koinonia is Acts 2:42 “They devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching and to the fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to prayer.” But the rest of the passage reads:  “ 43 Everyone was filled with awe at the many wonders and signs performed by the apostles. 44 All the believers were together and had everything in common. 45 They sold property and possessions to give to anyone who had need. 46 Every day they continued to meet together in the temple courts. They broke bread in their homes and ate together with glad and sincere hearts, 47 praising God and enjoying the favor of all the people. And the Lord added to their number daily those who were being saved.” Christian fellowship is a key aspect of the Christian life. Believers in Christ are to come together in love, faith, and encouragement. The essence of koinonia: “one another”. Scripture commands us to be devoted to one another (Romans 12:10), honor one another (Romans 12:10), live in harmony with one another (Romans 12:16; 1 Peter 3:8), accept one another (Romans 15:7), serve one another in love (Galatians 5:13), be kind and compassionate to one another (Ephesians 4:32), admonish one another (Colossians 3:16), encourage one another (1 Thessalonians 5:11; Hebrews 3:13), spur one another on toward love and good deeds (Hebrews 10:24), offer hospitality (1 Peter 4:9), and love one another (1 Peter 1:22; 1 John 3:11; 3:23; 4:7; 4:11-12). Koinonia is translated many different ways in English Bibles: -fellowship (koinonia), to the breaking of bread and the prayers.” -contribution (koinonia) for them and for all others.” Paul writes to the believers in Philippi: “That I may know him and the power of his resurrection, and may share (koinonia) his sufferings, becoming like him in his death” (Phil 3:10). – Christian living– the dynamic whole of it. It describes an interactive relationship between God and believers who are sharing new life through Christ.  It captures the entirety of this relationship. It involves active participation in Christian community: sharing in spiritual blessings and giving material blessings. How does this idea fit into the theology of ‘And’? Acts 1:8—it empowers us with the chisomo—the grace to DO—the all-inclusive– “But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes on you; and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth.” And they will know you by your love.  (John 13:35)   “By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you love one another.”

articles.title_zh: 契  约
articles.content: Isaiah 54:10  Though the mountains be shaken and the hills be removed, yet my unfailing love for you will not be shaken nor my covenant of peace be removed,” says the LORD, who has compassion on you. There is something of music in the very sound of these words. The thought that lies below them, sweeping as it does through the whole creation, and parting all things into the transient and eternal, the mortal and immortal, is still greater than the music of the words. ‘These’ are removed; ‘this’ abides. The thing in God which abides is all-gentle tenderness, that strange love mightier than all the powers of Deity beside, permanent with the permanence of His changeless heart. ‘My loving kindness and the covenant of My peace,’ outlast everything else. The antithesis of what passes and what abides is mind-boggling. ‘all things are in a state of flux’—it’s a basic tenant of physical science…and yet it seems as unchanging as anything we know…it’s the shape of the box…and yet,  if we had nothing abiding beyond this universe, what would be the point? There’s an unspoken  ‘But’  here–  in that vacuum, the Great Spirit moves all the material universe, Himself unmoved, undiminished by creation, or by said vacuum.  The Unknowable whose name means ‘breath’ is YHWH—who comes to us in man-form to help the created move toward and abide in this presence. I’m sort of blown away by how big this passage paints God…and blown away that we are His children…and that we able to abide because of Christ…that our part in glorifying Him and enjoying Him forever comes in walking alongside a global family and telling their stories.  Insignificant, by itself, but being used as a tool to help others abide and recognize the mercy and grace of this big Abba. We can touch the face of God…because He calls us to Himself.

articles.title_zh: Innocent As Doves
articles.content: The Scriptures Ephesians 6:10-18 (NIV) 10 Finally, be strong in the Lord and in his mighty power. 11 Put on the full armor of God, so that you can take your stand against the devil’s schemes. 12 For our struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the powers of this dark world and against the spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly realms. 13 Therefore put on the full armor of God, so that when the day of evil comes, you may be able to stand your ground, and after you have done everything, to stand. 14 Stand firm then, with the belt of truth buckled around your waist, with the breastplate of righteousness in place, 15 and with your feet fitted with the readiness that comes from the gospel of peace. 16 In addition to all this, take up the shield of faith, with which you can extinguish all the flaming arrows of the evil one. 17 Take the helmet of salvation and the sword of the Spirit,which is the word of God. 18 And pray in the Spirit on all occasions with all kinds of prayers and requests. With this in mind, be alert and always keep on praying for all the Lord’s people. Matthew 10:16-20 16 “I am sending you out like sheep among wolves. Therefore be as shrewd as snakes and as innocent as doves. 17 Be on your guard; you will be handed over to the local councils and be flogged in the synagogues. 18 On my account you will be brought before governors and kings as witnesses to them and to the Gentiles.19 But when they arrest you, do not worry about what to say or how to say it. At that time you will be given what to say, 20 for it will not be you speaking, but the Spirit of your Father speaking through you.” Today, it’s just been on my mind to bring our attention back to the armor of God and the fact we need to be wise like serpents, innocent as doves. I want to speak to the first part, being wise like serpents. Going to Malta helped bring to my attention how much I don’t know about my own country’s politics, the refugee crisis, trusting God, and even God’s word. I feel like I’m doing “better than the average U.S. citizen.” But, in reality, I don’t know very much. And I’ve realized when it comes to engaging in conversation with others, it’s important to have a handle on topics like these. I.e., talking with my dad about refugees. Having facts and knowing the what the constitution says helps me to better articulate and defend my stance culturally and based by our country’s laws. Knowing about the situation with refugees abroad also helps and is a tool in dispelling the fear which the current administration seems to use to get support to make the calls it’s trying to make both about refugees and immigrants in general. The second part, being innocent like doves…that’s a hard one for me because I’ve thought in the past it means to be naive. I don’t want to be naïve. But being innocent doesn’t mean you’re naïve. I think it means we guard our hearts and take our thoughts captive. What we put into our minds affects the lens through which we see the world and view the Bible—and it has the power to jade us. I.e., rape. I know rape is in the world. I know it is destructive. I’ve seen it damage lives. And I’ve seen God redeem. But, what I don’t need to do is read the part of a book or watch a TV series which details a situation of rape. I don’t need to invite that in my mind to “know” about rape. I’m thinking of a book one of my youth group girls was reading. I haven’t read it, but I see how she struggles with her sexuality, her relationship with God, and for a period even suicide. I also see how her parents are okay with exposing her to things that are a bit mature for her age. Compared to another one of our girls who is aware of what happens in the world, but her parents are careful to protect her from exposure to things which are dark, damaging, fracture her relationship with God. She’s being taught to be innocent, not naïve (or judgmental), and to take her thoughts captive. Both of these
articles.content_zh: 圣经以弗所书: 6: 10-18(NIV) 10 最后,要坚固于主和他强大的力量. 11 穿上上帝的全盔甲,以便你能够采取立场对抗魔鬼的阴谋. 12,因为我们的斗争不是反对血肉之争,而是反对统治者,反对当局,反对这个黑暗世界的力量,反对天界邪恶的精神力量. 13 因此穿上神的全甲,使出恶事之日到来后能站起地来,在做了一切后能站起地来. 14 站稳了, 真理带系住你的腰部, 胸罩是正义的, 15 和你的脚 与来自和平的福音的准备。 16,除此外,取起信道之盾,用之能灭一切恶道所发之火箭. 17取出救生之盔和"灵剑",这是"神之道". 18,并随各种祷告和请求,在"精神"中作各种祈祷. 考虑到这一点,保持警惕,并始终为主的所有人民祈祷。 Matthew 10:16-20 16 “我把你像羊一样放出狼群。 因此要像蛇一样精明,像鸽子一样无辜. 17 个 人 守 住 ; 交给 地方 议会 、 在 犹太会堂 被 鞭打 . 18,就我而言,你们将被带见总督和国王,作为他们和外邦人的见证。 19,但当他们逮捕你时,不要担心该说什么或怎么说. 在那日,你们得享受你们所应当享受的,20个是你们所应当享受的,只有你们父亲的精神。 今天,我刚刚想到让我们重新关注上帝的盔甲, 以及我们需要像蛇一样聪明, 我想谈谈第一部分,像蛇一样聪明。 前往马耳他让我注意到我对本国政治、难民危机、信任上帝甚至上帝之言一无所知。 我觉得自己比普通美国公民做得更好。 但事实上, 我意识到在与他人对话时, 和我爸谈难民的事 了解事实、了解宪法内容, 有助于我更好地表达和捍卫我的立场, 了解国外难民的情况,也有助于消除现政府似乎用来获得支持的恐惧, 第二部分是像鸽子一样无辜, 我不想天真。 但无辜并不意味着你天真。 我认为这意味着我们保护我们的心 并抓住我们的思想。 我们脑中的东西影响着我们通过这个镜头看到世界并看到圣经——它有制玉的力量。 强奸 我知道强奸在世界上。 我知道这是破坏性的。 我见过它会伤害生命。 我见过上帝赎回。 但我不需要阅读一本书或看一部电视连续剧, 我并不需要邀请她「知道」强奸事件。 我想到一本我的青年团体女孩正在阅读的书。 我还没读过, 但我看到她如何与性、与上帝的关系相抗争, 我也明白她的父母 让她面对一些对她的年龄来说有点成熟的事情是怎样的 和另外一位我们的女孩相比,她知道世界发生的事情,但她的父母很小心地保护她免受那些黑暗,有破坏力,断裂她与上帝关系的东西的暴露. 她被教导自己是无辜的, 两者

articles.title_zh: 亚伯拉罕和洛特
articles.content: Genesis 13 So Abram left Egypt and traveled north into the Negev, along with his wife and Lot and all that they owned. 2 (Abram was very rich in livestock, silver, and gold.) 3 From the Negev, they continued traveling by stages toward Bethel, and they pitched their tents between Bethel and Ai, where they had camped before. 4 This was the same place where Abram had built the altar, and there he worshiped the Lord again. 5 Lot, who was traveling with Abram, had also become very wealthy with flocks of sheep and goats, herds of cattle, and many tents. 6 But the land could not support both Abram and Lot with all their flocks and herds living so close together. 7 So disputes broke out between the herdsmen of Abram and Lot. (At that time Canaanites and Perizzites were also living in the land.) 8 Finally Abram said to Lot, “Let’s not allow this conflict to come between us or our herdsmen. After all, we are close relatives! 9 The whole countryside is open to you. Take your choice of any section of the land you want, and we will separate. If you want the land to the left, then I’ll take the land on the right. If you prefer the land on the right, then I’ll go to the left.” 10 Lot took a long look at the fertile plains of the Jordan Valley in the direction of Zoar. The whole area was well watered everywhere, like the garden of the Lord or the beautiful land of Egypt. (This was before the Lord destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah.) 11 Lot chose for himself the whole Jordan Valley to the east of them. He went there with his flocks and servants and parted company with his uncle Abram. 12 So Abram settled in the land of Canaan, and Lot moved his tents to a place near Sodom and settled among the cities of the plain. 13 But the people of this area were extremely wicked and constantly sinned against the Lord. 14 After Lot had gone, the Lord said to Abram, “Look as far as you can see in every direction—north and south, east and west. 15 I am giving all this land, as far as you can see, to you and your descendants[a] as a permanent possession. 16 And I will give you so many descendants that, like the dust of the earth, they cannot be counted! 17 Go and walk through the land in every direction, for I am giving it to you.” 18 So Abram moved his camp to Hebron and settled near the oak grove belonging to Mamre. There he built another altar to the Lord. At this point in the story, God’s promise to Abraham of the promised land hasn’t come true yet, but good land is part of the promise We’ve seen Abraham have faithful triumphs and failures, but this is a time when Abraham showed great faith once again because there are SEVERAL reasons why Abraham could have taken the better land 1. movement towards God’s promise of good land anyway 2. and this is probably a more striking one to me, but culturally speaking, the older would NEVER defer to the younger. Lot, as the younger, should have deferred to Abraham the older – both in going to him to resolve the disagreement between their herdsmen and in giving him the better pick of land But Abraham wasn’t fixated on culture and on manipulating God’s promises Abraham’s dealings are not in seniority, but in brotherly love and that’s what faith does. Faith resolves tension with generous self-sacrifice Christians often say in tense situations, “Well, I’m not a doormat! I deserve not to be walked all over!” But my pastor said something very striking to me. “Aren’t we glad Christ never said that?” A faithful and generous person doesn’t need to manipulate or control the situation because they are resting in the promises and sovereignty of God Faith leads to trust leads to generosity and self-sacrifice with others.
articles.content_zh: 创世记13 索·阿布拉姆从埃及出走,向北走入了内盖夫河,与他的妻子和洛特以及他们所拥有的一切. 2 (Abram有非常丰富的牲畜,白银和黄金. 3 他们从内盖夫出发,继续分步向贝瑟尔出行,在贝瑟尔和艾之间搭起帐篷,他们以前在那里扎营. 页:1 这是阿布拉姆建造祭坛的地方,在那里他再次崇拜了主. 5,当时正与阿布拉姆一起出行的洛特也变得非常富有了有羊羊群,牛群和许多帐篷. 6个 但土地无法支撑阿布拉姆和洛特 他们所有的羊群和群 生活如此相近。 第7条 亞伯蘭和魯特的牧民,互相爭論; (當時,迦南人和比瑞斯人同住), 8 最后,Abram对Lot说: " 让我们不要让这场冲突发生在我们和牧民之间。 我们毕竟是近亲! 第9条 整个农村都对你开放. 你选择你想要的土地的任何部分 我们就会分开 如果你想让土地在左边,那我就让土地在右边。 如果你喜欢右边的土地,那么我就往左边去。 10 洛特对约旦河谷向左尔方向的肥沃平原进行了长时间的考察. 整个地区到处都有良好的取水,如主的花园或埃及美丽的地. (这是在主毁灭了索多玛和戈莫拉之前) 11 洛特自己选择了他们以东的整个约旦河谷. 他带着他的羊群和仆人去那儿,和他叔叔Abram分道扬镳。 12日,阿布拉姆在迦南地定居,洛特将帐篷搬到了索多姆附近的一个地方,并定居于平地的城市中. 13,但此地之人,极恶而常犯主. 14 在洛特离开后,主对Abram说: " 请你看看每一个方向,即北和南、东和西。 15,我把所有的土地,就你所看到的,作为永久财产,交给你和你的子孙。 十六,我给你这么多的后人,像地上的尘土一样,他们不能被统计! 17 出行,走遍地上,各行各业,我把它赏赐你们。” 18日,阿布拉姆将营地迁至希伯伦并定居在属于马姆雷的橡树林附近. 在那里他又为主建造了一座祭坛. 在故事的这一刻,上帝对亚伯拉罕的允诺还没有实现,但好地是我们所见到的亚伯拉罕有忠实的胜利和失败的诺言的一部分,但此时亚伯拉罕再次表现出了极大的信心,因为有SEVERAL的理由,亚伯拉罕可以夺取更好的地一. 但从文化上讲, 年长者决不会屈从于年轻人。 作为年轻人,洛特应该把年长者留给亚伯拉罕 — — 既去他解决牧民之间的分歧,又让他选择更好的土地 — — 但亚伯拉罕并不热衷于文化和操纵上帝对亚伯拉罕的诺言 — — 亚伯拉罕的交往不是在资历上,而是在兄弟般的爱心上,而这正是信仰的作用。 信仰用慷慨自救的基督徒解决了紧张局势, 我不应该到处走! 但我的牧师对我说了一些非常引人注目的话。 “难道我们不庆幸基督从未这么说吗?” 一个忠诚而慷慨的人不需要操控或控制局势,因为他们沉浸在上帝信仰的承诺中,而主权导致信任导致与他人的慷慨和自我牺牲。

articles.title_zh: 神的安慰
articles.content: My family still wrestles with what feels like very fresh grief over my dad’s passing last September. There are moments where things hit us and we feel this ache of his absence. We know that he has gone to be with his Heavenly Father and no longer suffers from the limitations of this mortal coil. It’s just that sometimes, we miss him. It’s at those times when something happens that reminds us of the hope that we have in Christ our Savior, of our purpose here as followers of Christ, as co-laborers in the Kingdom of Heaven. These reminders serve as encouragement to fight the good fight, keeping our eyes on the prize. I was thinking of my dad today and decided to read some of the devotionals he used to write for the ministry to which he dedicated his remaining years, Transport for Christ. When his health could no longer allow him to serve onsite as a chaplain, he wrote encouragement to the truck drivers and the chaplains in service. I can hear his voice in these words. There’s great comfort in his reminder. I share his words with you so that you may also take comfort in a greater plan, and in the hope that comes from trusting God is in control: “Most of the time, when we grieve, we grieve over something that’s happened in our lives. But there are also times when we grieve over something that hasn’t happened or “what might have been.” Unrealized expectations and dashed hopes can paralyze us with sadness. We mourn for what we could have had, could have done or could have experienced. We live in a fog as we struggle with our unmet goals and dreams. Are you wrestling with accepting something in your life? Mourning a shattered dream? Instead of focusing on what might have been, try focusing on what is and what could still be. Revising your dreams isn’t bad. It’s realistic. And the sooner you do, the sooner the weight of grief will let go. The fog will lift. Hope will return.”
articles.content_zh: 我父亲去年九月去世, 有些时候 事情袭击了我们 我们感到他缺席很痛苦 我们知道他和他天父在一起 不再受到这个凡人圈子的限制 只是有时候,我们想念他。 我们的救世主, 我们作为基督的追随者, 这些提醒有助于鼓励我们打好这场好仗,使我们继续关注这一奖项。 我今天想到我爸,决定读一些他以前为他剩下的岁月所奉献的部会而作的奉献,"为基督而运输". 当他的健康不能再允许他当上牧师时,他写信给正在服役的卡车司机和牧师。 这些话我都能听到他的声音。 他提醒大家, 我和你们分享他的话,以便你们也能在更大的计划中得到安慰,希望来自信任上帝的希望是控制着:“多数时候,当我们悲伤的时候,我们对生活中发生的事情感到悲伤。 但有时我们也为一些没有发生的事情而悲伤, 未实现的期望和破灭的希望会使我们感到悲哀。 我们对本可以、本可以或本可以经历的事情表示哀悼。 当我们与未实现的目标和梦想相抗争时,我们生活在雾中。 你是在拼命接受你生活中的东西吗? 打破了梦想? 与其专注于可能已经发生的事情,不如专注于现在和可能仍然可能发生的事情。 改变你的梦想并不坏。 这是现实的。 你越早做, 悲伤的重量会越快松开。 雾会升起 希望将回归。”

articles.title: A chance meeting?
articles.summary: You’ve probably heard someone say ‘There is no such thing as a coincidence’. Usually people nod their heads and murmur agreement, but the real question is “Do you believe it?“...
articles.summary_zh: 您可能听说过有人说“没有所谓的巧合”。通常人们会点头低语，但真正的问题是“你相信吗？” ……
articles.title_zh: 一相逢
articles.content: You’ve probably heard someone say ‘There is no such thing as a coincidence’. Usually people nod their heads and murmur agreement, but the real question is “Do you believe it?“ Are people just wishful thinkers, or is God really so intimately involved in our daily lives that He orchestrate events on our behalf? What will a chance meeting turn into later? The idea of seeds, planting and harvest is a theme resonant throughout Scripture. Aside from the overt nature of sharing the hope of Christ, there are times we don’t recognize an opportunity at the time, but hindsight has a way of revealing it to us. On my last day in Cairo, I was sitting in the hotel lobby waiting for the rest of the team to come down for checkout. I opened my laptop, and began weeding through emails, and getting pictures uploaded for post, and checking through Facebook. An older gentleman (whom I’d seen at different times all week) came over and said ‘You work too much’. I told him I was just killing time and not really working at all. He began asking me questions about my visit to Cairo. Given the upset of the country, I was still guarding my words very carefully so as not to endanger people who live and minister in Cairo. He began asking more pointed questions like “What do you think of this revolution?” Alarm bells were ringing in my head, so I trod very carefully as I answered. I told him that it was a very exciting time in Egypt’s history. Nothing would ever be the same for the country again. To be here during this growth period was both exhilarating and a little scary. He then asked what my friends thought of the goings on. Now, here I had to be very careful. I asked God for wisdom and told him that depended on who I spoke with. There were some who were very optimistic about the outcome, although they knew there would be a hard period to get there. Others were very pessimistic and a little fearful about what lay ahead for them. Still others were moving forward in confidence. He nodded a few times as I responded to his question, then said, “You should come to Lebanon.” I responded “I would LOVE to come to Lebanon!” So he handed me his business card and said, “E-mail me when you come.” He wrote his email address on the bottom of the card. Initially, I was wary about taking some stranger’s e-mail, but I figured I would not necessarily use it and I did not have to respond by giving him my e-mail. We stood, shook hands and parted. I noted that as he left, he entered a diplomat’s vehicle. Only then did I read his business card. It read “Mahmoud Hammoud, Lebanese Ambassador”. He’s the former Foreign Minister of Lebanon, currently serving as an ambassador. I have no idea why our paths crossed. However, God orchestrated it for some reason. There are no coincidences…just opportunities. I wonder what comes next.
articles.content_zh: 你可能已经听到有人说“没有巧合”了。 通常人们点头并含糊其辞,但真正的问题是“你相信吗?” 难道人们只是希望的思想家,还是上帝真的如此亲密地参与我们的日常生活,以至于他代表我们组织各种活动? 机会会议以后会变成什么? 种子、种植和收割的理念是贯穿整个圣经的主题。 除了分享基督希望的公开性质外, 有时我们并不认同当时的机会, 在开罗的最后一天,我坐在酒店大厅里,等待队伍的其他人下来看病。 我打开了笔记本电脑, 开始通过电子邮件去除草, 一位年长的绅士(我整个星期在不同时间见过他)过来说道:你工作太忙了。 我告诉他我只是在浪费时间 完全没有工作 他开始问我关于我访问开罗的问题。 鉴于这个国家的不安,我仍在非常谨慎地捍卫我的话,以免危及在开罗生活和担任部长的人。 他开始提出更尖锐的问题,如“你对这场革命的看法如何?” 警钟在我脑中响起,所以我回答时非常小心。 我告诉他,这是埃及历史上一个非常激动人心的时刻。 对这个国家来说,一切都不会变了 在这个成长时期来到这里既令人振奋,又有些吓人。 他接着问我的朋友们对事情的看法如何。 现在,我必须非常小心。 我向上帝求取智慧 告诉他这取决于我和谁说话 有些人对结果非常乐观,尽管他们知道要到达那里会有一段困难的时期。 其他人则非常悲观,有些担心未来会如何。 还有一些国家正在以信任的态度向前迈进。 当我回答他的问题时,他点了几次头,然后说:“你应该来黎巴嫩。” 我回应说, 他把他的名片递给我,然后说:“你来了就给我电子邮件。” 他写了他的电子邮件地址 在卡底。 起初,我对收取陌生人的电子邮件很担心,但我想我不一定会使用,我不必通过把电子邮件给他来回应。 我们站了起来,握起手来分开。 我注意到,当他离开时,他进入一名外交官的车辆。 那时我才看他的名片 原文为“黎巴嫩大使马哈穆德·哈穆德”。 现任大使。 我不知道我们为什么要过路 然而,上帝出于某种原因安排了它。 没有巧合 只是机会 不知道接下来会怎样

articles.title: What comes first: chicken or the egg?
articles.summary: One thing I am noticing here is how different the context of ministry is from country to country. You can sometimes THINK you understand the concept of the vehicle, like...
articles.summary_zh: 我在这里注意到的一件事是，不同国家的事工背景是多么的不同。有时您可能会认为自己了解车辆的概念，例如...
articles.title_zh: 先吃鸡还是先吃鸡蛋？
articles.content: One thing I am noticing here is how different the context of ministry is from country to country. MNN's Ruth Kramer on assignment. You can sometimes THINK you understand the concept of the vehicle, like micro-enterprise, but once you hear how things are put into practice, what works and what doesn’t, you begin to see the subtleties emerge. For example, we met with a partner yesterday who assists community development. They are unashamedly Christian, because the Gospel is part of everything they do…however, they know that dealing with poverty is a ‘must’, as well. So, which came first, the chicken (community development) or the egg (Gospel)? Can they be done simultaneously and be effective? Do you really just have two eggs or two chickens? The clear answer on that was: ‘We have an egg, it becomes a chicken’. Folks, that’s the answer to the question of questions. The hope of Christ changes the outlook for the poor in this context. The other big question was how the community development works in the Egyptian Muslim context in the rural areas. It is in these places where it’s likely opposition will rise up and equate physical attacks. The mindset is quite different. Micro-enterprise comes up at this point. In some Asian countries, the structure of a micro-enterprise program works like this: church committee sees community member in need (often a believer under the discipleship of the pastor), they provide a loan so this person can start a small business–i.e.—buy a sewing machine to make clothes, or a couple of goats to make cheese and sell milk…from the profits, the person tithes to the church, enabling the support of the pastor…and the person is more able to support him/herself. However, when I asked about the structure of the micro-enterprise, it can’t work that way in the Egyptian context. There are lots of things that can really be misinterpreted within the social structure (and Islam) and this is one of them. The set up of the program is similar, but different because it’s tailor-made to fit the need of the people and the mission of the group. That just struck me. I had made an assumption that all micro-enterprise was the same. I made similar assumptions about vocational training programs, literacy programs, etc (thinking I adjusting for a different context, language, etc). I think it’s kind of a colonialistic thinking that we slip into. It’s kind of like providing someone a loaf of bread (mission field)…from the grocery store (missionary). They need the food to stay alive, but the plastic around the bread is giving them indigestion. They need to prepare the bread the way they now how and all we need to do is supply the ingredients (resources) and the recipe (training). Yes, I know you might be thinking ‘well, duh’. It is one thing to say it and to think you might even understand it, it is another thing entirely to actually see it with my own eyes, hear what works and what doesn’t from the guys implementing helps. By the way, because they do this work well, they have just come under scrutiny. One of this ministry’s main offices was raided by the Egyptian government this week, and the hard drive with the database was taken. All of their records on every program were on it. Everything is exposed. Their face is an NGO and they are well-known. With the events that have occurred in Egypt over the last month, it’s no surprise they’re looking at all NGO’s. Please pray for this team. They are careful, and they are smart. Most of all, they want to share the hope of Christ with those they encounter. That love for people permeates everything they touch…including the chickens in the coop…and eggs in the community. Works for me…
articles.content_zh: 我在这里注意到的一件事是,部委的背景因国而异。 MNN的Ruth Kramer在执行任务 你有时可以认为你理解汽车的概念, 比如微型企业, 但一旦你听到事情是如何付诸实践的, 什么可行什么不可行, 你就会开始看到微妙之处的出现。 例如,我们昨天会见了一个协助社区发展的伙伴。 他们毫不羞愧地信奉基督教, 因为福音书是他们所做的一切的一部分. 那么,什么是第一位的, 鸡(社区发展)还是蛋(Gospel)? 它们能否同时进行并有效? 你真的有两只蛋还是两只鸡? 答案是:我们有一个鸡蛋,它变成了一只鸡。 各位,这就是问题答案。 基督的希望改变了穷人在这方面的前景。 另一个大问题是社区发展如何在农村地区埃及穆斯林背景下运作。 这些地方很可能会有人反对, 心态完全不同。 此时小微企业也出现了. 在一些亚洲国家,微型企业计划的结构是这样运作的:教会委员会看到社区成员有需要(常常是牧师门徒下的信徒),他们提供贷款,以便此人能够创办小企业,即购买缝纫机来做衣服,或买一对山羊来做起司和卖牛奶. 从利润中,一个人一分之一到教堂,使牧师能够支持.这个人更有能力支持自己。 然而,当我问到微型企业的结构时,在埃及不可能如此。 在社会结构(和伊斯兰教)中, 有许多事情可以真正被误解, 节目的设置类似,但因适合人民的需要和团体的使命而有所不同. 这让我很吃惊 我假设所有微型企业都是一样的 我对职业培训计划,扫盲计划等做出了类似的假设(认为我适应不同的环境,语言等). 我认为我们滑入的是一种殖民主义思想。 像是从杂货店(Missionary)提供面包。 他们需要食物才能活下来 但面包周围的塑料 让他们消化不良 他们需要用他们现在的方式准备面包,我们需要做的就是提供原料(资源)和食谱(培训)。 是的,我知道你可能在想,“好,好” 并且认为你可能甚至能理解, 以我自己的眼光亲眼目睹, 顺便说一句,因为他们做得很好,他们刚刚受到审查。 埃及政府本周突袭了该部的一个主要办公室, 他们在每个程序上的所有记录都在上面。 一切众生被所出. 他们的外表是非政府组织,是众所周知的。 在埃及上个月发生的事件中, 请为这支队伍祈祷. 他们很小心,很聪明。 最重要的是,他们想与所遭遇的人分享基督的希望. 这种对人的爱贯穿了他们所接触的一切... 包括笼子里的鸡... 和社区的鸡蛋. 为我工作...

articles.title_zh: 释放祈祷的力量
articles.content: Last night, I attended a prayer meeting at a church in downtown Cairo, near Tahrir Square. MNN in Egypt The church was gathering to cry out to God in their distress over the recent events in the country, and cry out, they did. As we sang together, worshiped together, and encouraged one another, I experienced something I have never experienced before. I’m a fairly reserved person and I am even more so in prayer. It is in times of great distress that I get out of my own way and fall before the Lord prostrate. Last night, although everyone around me was praying in Arabic, I found myself humbled before the Lord and joining in that chorus of crying out. The pastor was beyond ‘crying out’….he was screaming and sobbing before the Lord, as was much of this nearly 1,000 person gathering. Here they were, in prayer before God, confessing, repenting, requesting and rejoicing…even as tear gas seeped into the courtyard from Tahrir Square. All of a sudden, I found myself reminding God of His promises, and asking Him to give comfort to His bride in Egypt, to give them hope and wisdom and to be asking with a fierceness I had not ever before encountered…and moments later, the pastor or worship leader would be saying the same thing, or using the same verse, or introducing the song on the same topic…that happened over and over last night. An immediate confirmation of God’s response left me stunned. Much of what I have heard from Egypt’s Christians that I have encountered has been this is a year of prophecy coming true. There is a GREAT confidence in many of the church leaders and congregations in forging ahead… The other thing that we’re often hearing is that Egypt’s Church is not ‘persecuted’ so much as it is a church under pressure. The boldness of this family is so encouraging, and such a reminder of the presence of the Holy Spirit…especially as they go out with joy to tend to the wounded people coming into the field hospital set up in their courtyard. The confirmation of God’s answers to prayer gives a great boldness to those on the frontlines of the missional movement in Egypt. While bombings, riots and general chaos looks really bad in the headlines (and it is happening), fear is not the response of this emboldened Body. Church leaders we have met with all over the city have said the same thing ‘The wall of fear is broken’. Change is coming. Egypt will have her Revolution…and its face is the Church.
articles.content_zh: 昨晚,我参加了在开罗市中心的一座教堂举行的祈祷会,该教堂靠近塔里尔广场. 埃及的MNN 教会正在集会 向上帝呼喊 在他们的痛苦 最近的国内事件, 当我们一起唱歌,一起崇拜,互相鼓励时,我经历了一些我从未经历过的事情. 我是一个相当有保留的人, 是在大难之时,我走出了自己的道路,倒向了主的叩头. 昨晚,虽然我周围的每个人都用阿拉伯语祈祷,但我发现自己在主面前谦卑并加入了那场叫喊的合唱. 牧师已经超越了“哭出声来”的范围, 他们在这里向上帝祈祷,忏悔、悔改、请求并欢欣鼓舞, 突然间,我发现自己提醒了上帝他的承诺,要求他安慰他的埃及新娘,给他们以希望和智慧,并以我从未遇到过的激烈要求. . . 立即确认上帝的反应,使我感到震惊。 我从埃及基督徒那里听到的大多是今年的预言。 许多教会领袖和会众对前进充满信心... 我们经常听到的另外一件事是,埃及的教会并没有像压力下的一个教会那样被 " 迫害 " 。 这个家庭的胆量是如此鼓舞人心,如此地提醒着圣灵的存在...... 特别是当他们欢快地出门去照顾受伤的人进入他们院子里建立的野外医院时. 在埃及传教运动的前线, 虽然爆炸、暴动和普遍混乱在头条新闻上看起来非常糟糕(而且正在发生), 我们与全市的教会领袖都说过同样的话:恐惧之墙被打破了。 变化即将到来。 埃及将会有她的革命... 它的脸是教会。

articles.title: Five Ways to Pray for Persecuted Christians
articles.summary: Jamie Dean offers a prayer guide for persecuted Christians in Iran, China, North Korea, and other hard to reach nations.
articles.summary_zh: 杰米·迪恩（ Jamie Dean ）为伊朗、中国、朝鲜和其他难以抵达的国家的受迫害基督徒提供了祈祷指南。
articles.title_zh: 为受迫害的基督徒祈祷的五种方式
articles.content: Sunday, Nov. 1, marks the annual International Day of Prayer for the Persecuted Church. It’s a day for believers across the globe to unite in concentrated prayer for Christians suffering for the gospel. Here are a few biblically-based ways to pray for the persecuted, along with a guide to a few specific nations to remember. 1. PRAY FOR THOSE IN PRISON “Remember those who are in prison, as though in prison with them.” Hebrews 13:3 Iran : In 2025, Christians were sentenced to a combined total of more than 280 years in prison . Pray for those still in jail, and for families enduring separation. China : The Chinese government has continued its crackdown on believers, including several still in prison after a raid on Zion Church last year . Pray for gospel hope and perseverance. Eritrea : As many as 350 believers remained in jails in 2025, including some who have been imprisoned for decades . Pray for endurance and deliverance. 2. PRAY FOR BOLDNESS “And now, Lord, look upon their threats and grant to your servants to continue to speak your word with all boldness.” Acts 4: 29 Syria, Pakistan , Libya , Sudan : Danger and threats are a common experience for believers in these nations. Pray for the Lord to protect churches and give them boldness to proclaim Christ, even when it’s difficult. 3. PRAY THAT PEOPLE WILL COME TO KNOW JESUS “I want you to know, brothers, that what has happened to me has really served to advance the gospel.” Philippians 1:12 Afghanistan : In a country where it’s more dangerous than ever to follow Jesus, Afghans are still coming to know him. Pray believers will continue to be a witness, and that unbelievers will find true life in Christ. 4. PRAY FOR GOD’S BLESSING TO THOSE SUFFERING “Blessed are those who are persecuted for righteousness’ sake, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven…Rejoice and be glad, for your reward is great in heaven.” Matthews 5:10,12 North Korea, Somalia, Yemen: These are among the most difficult places in the world to follow Christ. Pray for the Lord to bless these believers facing severe persecution, and to strengthen them with the hope of heaven. 5. PRAY FOR THE PERSECUTORS “Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you.” Matthew 5:44 Nigeria: Christians in northern Nigeria have endured kidnappings and violence for years. Pray the Lord will stop their attackers, and use the believers’ witness to draw persecutors to himself. For more ways to pray for the persecuted church, grab a copy of Pray the World , a 31-day devotional for hard to reach nations.

articles.title: Standing with Brothers and Sisters We Cannot See
articles.summary: David Platt shares a powerful story of forgiveness and challenges Christians to support persecuted believers through prayer.
articles.summary_zh: 大卫·普拉特（ David Platt ）分享了一个关于宽恕的强大故事，并挑战基督徒通过祈祷来支持受迫害的信徒。
articles.title_zh: 与我们看不到的兄弟姐妹站在一起
articles.content: I remember the first time I stood at the demilitarized zone, or the DMZ, on the border between North and South Korea. I looked across this dividing line, knowing that on the other side I (and we) have brothers and sisters who are suffering and dying for following Jesus and making him known. I think about Soon Yangown, a pastor in a leper colony during the Japanese occupation of the Korean peninsula many years ago. He refused to worship the shrines that had been set up for the Korean people to worship, so he was arrested and imprisoned. When the Japanese occupation ended, he was released. Years later, his two oldest sons, Tongin and Tongsin, were in middle school when a mob representing the communist party came to their campus. The boys were known to be strong Christians, so the mob brought them out of the school and began to beat them. Eventually, a leader of the mob named Ahn shot and killed both the boys. By the time Pastor Soon heard of his sons’ death, the revolt had been quieted, and his sons’ killer had been apprehended. Upon hearing this news, Pastor Soon immediately sent a messenger to the court to plead for them to spare Ahn. The judge agreed to do so, and Pastor Soon then offered to adopt Ahn as his own son. Years later, communists invaded the leper colony where Pastor Soon was pastoring. He refused to flee and chose to stay with the church. He was arrested, imprisoned, tied up with 75 other followers of Jesus, and executed. I wish these stories were only from the past. Unfortunately, however, suffering, persecution, and martyrdom are present-day realities for our brothers and sisters in North Korea. So what can we do for them? For starters, we can remember them and learn about what they are experiencing. In the words of Hebrews 13:3: “Remember those who are in prison, as though in prison with them, and those who are mistreated, since you also are in the body.” We can take time to listen to and learn the story of our family in North Korea as if we were with them in North Korea. (Radical’s documentary Hard to Reach: North Korea is a good place to start.) As you remember our brothers and sisters in North Korea and other hard lands , I invite you to pray for them. Let your prayers be guided by Paul’s exhortation in Ephesians 6:18–20 for the church to pray for him while he was in prison: “To that end, keep alert with all perseverance, making supplication for all the saints, and also for me, that words may be given to me in opening my mouth boldly to proclaim the mystery of the gospel, for which I am an ambassador in chains, that I may declare it boldly, as I ought to speak.” Finally, let’s join them. They’re giving their lives to share the gospel with people around them. If you’re reading this, the likelihood is that your life is not at stake in the same way as theirs. But you can still give your life to what they’re giving their lives to: speaking the gospel and sharing God’s love in Jesus with the people you and I interact with today. Let’s lock arms with our brothers and sisters in North Korea , following Jesus and making him known no matter what it costs, because we know that he is our reward. This article first appeared in The Commission , Radical’s biweekly newsletter featuring global gospel stories and encouragement from David Platt and others to help you follow Jesus and make him known. Subscribe today .
articles.content_zh: 我记得我第一次站在非军事区,即位于南北朝鲜边境的非军事区。 我越过了这个分界线,知道在另一边,我(和我们)有兄弟姐妹,他们因追随耶稣并让他出名而受苦受难并死去. 我想起在多年前日本占领朝鲜半岛期间,一个麻风病殖民地的牧师Soon Yangown。 他拒绝为朝鲜人民所崇拜而设置的神社,于是被捕入狱. 日本占领结束后被放出. 多年后,他的两个最年长的儿子通仁和通辛在中学就读,当时一个代表共产主义政党的暴徒来到了他们的校园. 男孩们已知是坚固的基督徒,于是暴徒将他们从学校带出并开始殴打他们. 最终,一个暴徒的领袖命名 安开枪打死了两个男孩 在Sonon牧师听到他儿子的死讯时,叛乱已经平息,杀害他儿子的凶手已被逮捕。 在听到这个消息后,索恩牧师立即派使者去朝廷恳求他们放过安. 法官同意这样做,而索恩牧师随后提出收养安为自己的儿子. 多年后,共产主义分子入侵了"索恩牧师"正在作牧师的麻风病人聚居地. 他拒绝出逃,选择留在教堂. 他被逮捕,入狱,被绑起与另外75名耶稣追随者,被处死. 我希望这些故事只是从过去。 然而,不幸的是,对我们北朝鲜的兄弟姐妹来说,痛苦、迫害和殉道是当今的现实。 我们能为他们做什么? 首先,我们可以记住他们,了解他们正在经历的一切。 用希伯来人13:3的话来说:“记住那些在狱中的人,好像在狱中一样,以及那些受到虐待的人,因为你也是在身体里。” 我们可以花时间聆听和学习我们家在朝鲜的故事,就像我们在朝鲜与他们在一起一样. (Radical的纪录片"难去难去":朝鲜是个好起点. ) 我邀请你为他们祈祷。 保罗在《以弗所书6:18-20》中劝告教会在狱中为他祈祷:“为此,请全心全意地为所有圣人祈祷,也为我祈祷,愿为我大胆地开口宣讲福音之谜,因为我是一个被锁住的大使,让我大胆地宣示福音之谜。 最后,让我们加入他们。 他们献出生命与周围的人分享福音。 如果你读到这个, 你的生命可能与他们的生命不同。 你仍然可以把生命献给他们所付出的:说出福音,与你我今天交往的人分享上帝对耶稣的爱。 让我们和朝鲜的兄弟姐妹们握起手来, 这篇文章首次刊登在委员会的双周通讯《激进》上, 今日订阅.

articles.title: How Missionaries Should Serve Where Churches Already Exist
articles.summary: Brian Pate explains how missionaries can equip national churches to mature, reproduce, and plant healthy churches for generations.
articles.summary_zh: 布莱恩·佩特（ Brian Pate ）解释了传教士如何让国家教会成熟、繁殖和种植健康的教会。
articles.title_zh: 传教士应该如何在教会已经存在的地方服务
articles.content: I’m a missionary in Brazil , and I’m surrounded by churches—Baptist, Presbyterian, Nazarene, Assembly of God—the list goes on and on. Brazil has a rich history of missionaries who left a legacy of churches that are now sending missionaries to other countries. This raises a question: Should we send missionaries to countries where churches already exist? Shouldn’t we consider those regions “reached” and send our resources into more needy areas of the world? It’s a fair question, and worth exploring. Before we land on an answer, here are a few factors to consider: REMEMBER THE EXAMPLE OF PAUL Didn’t Paul say his mission was to reach those who had never heard the gospel (Rom 15:20)? Yes, a significant part of Paul’s ministry was as a church-planting missionary. But he did not abandon these newly planted churches. Paul was also a church-strengthening missionary. He revisited the churches he planted (Acts 14:21–23; 15:36; 18:22–23). He wrote letters to these churches because there was more that he needed to teach them (1 Thess 3:10). He even sent out his own missionary workers to areas he had previously reached: Tychichus to Ephesus and Colossae, Titus to Corinth, Crete, and Dalmatia, and Timothy to Ephesus and other cities. Surprisingly, we don’t have any record of Paul sending missionaries to unreached areas, but only to areas he had already reached. Paul creates helpful categories for us. We see Romans 15 pioneer missions, but we also see Acts 14 church-strengthening missions. Should we send missionaries where churches already exist? Paul shows us there is a biblical category for missions like this . In fact, Paul did it. CONSIDER THE HEALTH OF THE CHURCHES As I have trained pastors over the years, I have encountered alarming situations: churches that tolerate immorality, pastors who fail to understand the simple gospel message, and church leaders who unknowingly regurgitate heresy to their congregation. In my denomination, many churches are either embracing prosperity theology or depending on pragmatism to fulfill the Great Commission . Yes, I’m surrounded by “churches”, but when we only consider truly evangelical churches, the list is much smaller. And if we want to further whittle it down to healthy churches, the number gets very slim. Consider the health of the churches. If we neglect “reached” fields, we run the risk of creating new unreached people groups in just a few generations. UNDERSTAND THE NEEDS OF GOSPEL INFRASTRUCTURE So, what is the role of a missionary in a “reached” country? It is helpful to consider the missionary’s role in the big picture of what God is already doing in that country. This is where the rubric of gospel infrastructure is so helpful. Think of it this way: A city needs to put certain structures in place (such as road networks, water supply, and energy grids), so that it can continue to exist and thrive in the future. Similarly, the Great Commission requires far more than initial evangelism. For a national church to grow and reproduce, it will need to have “gospel infrastructure” in place. This begins with evangelism, Bible translation, and planting healthy churches, but also includes Christian literature, local pastor training, local worship music, and seminaries. The missions task involves everything a national church needs, so they can continue planting healthy churches for generations to come. When sending missionaries to areas that already have churches, we need to ask where the missionary’s gifts and the national church’s needs intersect. For example, Brazil probably does not need missionaries to plant more churches, but there are still great needs in the areas of seminaries and local pastor training. MISSIONS WHERE CHURCHES ALREADY EXIST? Should we send missionaries where churches already exist? Based on Paul’s own example, the answer is yes. We should continue sending Great Commission workers anywhere there is the need for healthy churches and gospel infrastructure. May we joyfully serve in
articles.content_zh: 我在巴西是传教士, 我周围是教堂, 巴西有丰富的传教士历史,他们留下了现在向其他国家派遣传教士的教会遗产. 这提出了一个问题:我们是否应该派遣传教士到已经存在教堂的国家去? 我们不应该认为那些地区已经“到达”了, 这是一个公平的问题, 在回答之前, 有几个因素需要考虑: 记得PAUL的ExAMPLE吗? 对,保罗部相当一部分是教会的传教士。 但他并没有放弃这些被新建的教堂. 保罗也是一名加强教会的传教士. 他重新审视了所种植的教堂(第14:21-23;15:36;18:22-23号法案)。 他给这些教堂写了信,因为他需要更多的教他们(1 Thess 3:10). 他甚至派遣了自己的传教工人去他之前所到的地区:提奇丘斯去以弗所和克洛斯塞,提图斯去科林斯,克勒特去和达尔马提亚去,提摩西去以弗所等城市去. 令人惊讶的是,我们没有任何保罗派遣传教士前往未到达的地区的记录,而只是前往他已经到达的地区。 保罗为我们创造了有用的类别。 我们看到罗马人的15个先锋任务,但我们也看到14号行动加强教堂的任务。 我们是否应该派传教士到已经存在教堂的地方? 保罗向我们展示了一个圣经类的任务。 事实上,保罗做到了。 考虑中国的健康 这些年来,我训练了牧师,我遇到了令人震惊的情况:教会容忍不道德,牧师不理解简单的福音信息,教会领导人不知不觉地把异端归罪于他们的教会。 许多教会要么接受繁荣神学, 但当我们只考虑真正福音派教会时, 如果我们想把它进一步切入到健康的教堂里, 数字变得非常微弱。 考虑教会的健康。 如果我们忽视“接触”领域,我们就有可能在短短几代人中产生新的未接触人群。 理解政府基础设施的需要 因此,传教士在“传入”国家的作用是什么? 在大背景下考虑传教士对上帝在该国已经采取的行动的作用是有益的。 这是福音基础设施的特色 如此有帮助。 这样想:一个城市需要建立某些结构(如道路网、供水和能源网),以便它能够继续存在并在未来兴起。 同样地,大委员会要求的远远不止于最初的福音. 国家教会要发展和再生,就必须建立“神道基础设施”。 这开始于福音会,圣经翻译,并种植健康的教堂,但也包括了基督教文学,地方牧师培训,地方崇拜音乐,和神学院. 任务涉及国家教会需要的一切,因此他们可以继续为后代种植健康的教堂. 当派遣传教士前往已经拥有教堂的地区时,我们需要问传教士的礼物和全国教会的需求在哪里交叉. 例如,巴西可能不需要传教士来种植更多的教堂,但在神学院和地方牧师培训方面仍有巨大的需要. 任务 Churches已经存在 我们是否应该派传教士到已经存在教堂的地方? 根据保罗自己的例子,答案是肯定的。 我们应继续派遣大委员会的工人到任何需要健康教堂和福音基础设施的地方去。 愿我们愉快地服务于

articles.title: How Ordinary Christians Can Help Others Follow Jesus
articles.summary: Salvador Blanco-Perello shows how everyday activities can become opportunities to help others follow Jesus.
articles.summary_zh: Salvador Blanco-Perello展示了日常活动如何成为帮助他人跟随耶稣的机会。
articles.title_zh: 普通基督徒如何帮助他人跟随耶稣
articles.content: Ask a handful of Christians to define “discipling,” and you’ll probably get a handful of different answers . Some may mention meeting with another follower of Jesus for an hour each week. Another might say it means attending the weekly Sunday school class on discipleship. Someone else says it involves teaching another Christian how to make disciples who disciple others . But ultimately, discipling others means giving someone access to your life. That’s how Jesus did it. Jesus’ whole life was a teaching moment for his disciples. Not only the miraculous parts of his life, but the ordinary ones too. The times in between: walking, talking, eating. This approach is often inconvenient, but it was the key ingredient to Jesus’ discipleship plan. I want to propose a simple principle for discipling: bring someone with you. Sure, there’s more to discipling, but you won’t disciple anyone if you don’t bring anyone along to what you’re already doing as a follower of Jesus. Call it discipling as double-duty. Imagine what it could look like. By doing something as simple as sitting in worship with someone, you may learn how to serve your own family better. Perhaps you’ll see how a young father serves his wife by taking the baby out so his wife can focus on the sermon or prayers. Perhaps you’ll be able to model your own worship habits. Corporate worship is a form of discipling. In fact, it’s the center from which all discipling flows . We learn to worship Jesus privately as we learn from other Christians publicly. Don’t miss on what you can teach or learn by observing Christians around you before, during, and after worship services. Or perhaps you can bring someone along to a community group to sing, pray, bear each other’s burdens, and apply the sermon more deeply to their lives. By bringing a person you’re discipling or being discipled by, perhaps you both learn new forms of hospitality . Maybe you learn how to disagree more lovingly and patiently. You learn to rejoice with those who rejoice and weep with those who weep. You could also bring someone along as you evangelize . Often, Christians don’t know how to evangelize because they’ve simply never seen another Christian do it. Does the person you disciple have a chance to see how you might share the gospel with someone? Even if you do all these things, someone you’re discipling must be able to see your walk with Jesus in order to replicate what they see in everyday life. The disciples didn’t just see Jesus preach the Sermon on the Mount . They saw the moments in between. They saw not only how he taught, but what he did after he taught. Jesus did say: “Therefore whoever relaxes one of the least of these commandments and teaches others to do the same will be called least in the kingdom of heaven, but whoever does them and teaches them will be called great in the kingdom of heaven” (Matt. 5:19). Discipling as double-duty will mean bringing someone along with you to the most ordinary moments of life. It will involve both teaching and doing what Christ commands. On the grocery run. The walk around the neighborhood. The car ride when you’d rather listen to music. As you bring other followers of Jesus with you into your existing rhythms of following Jesus, don’t underestimate what God might be teaching others. All of life following Jesus can be an opportunity to disciple others. Maybe the question shouldn’t be: “How can I make more time to disciple others?” But instead: “How can I use the time I have to disciple others?” Everybody does not have time for everybody, but everybody has time for somebody.
articles.content_zh: 让少数基督徒定义“纪律”, 有些人可能提到每周会和另一个耶稣的追随者会面一小时. 另一种说法可能表示,这意味着参加每周一次的"周日"学校的门徒会. 有人说,这涉及到教另一个基督徒 如何使门徒谁门徒。 但归根结底,管教别人意味着 给别人进入你的生活。 耶稣就是这样做的。 耶稣一生都是他的门徒们的教诲时刻. 不仅是他生命中的奇迹 也是普通的 中间的时代:行走,说话,吃. 这种做法往往不方便,但它是耶稣的门徒计划的关键要素。 我想提出一个简单的纪律原则:带一个人来。 当然,还有更多的纪律约束,但如果你不把任何人带到你作为耶稣的追随者已经在做的事情上,你就不会门徒。 称其为"纪律"为"双重义务". 想象一下它会是什么样子。 通过做一些简单的事情, 和别人一起礼拜, 你可以学习如何更好地为自己的家庭服务。 可能你会看到年轻父亲如何为妻子服务, 或许你可以模仿自己的崇拜习惯。 企业崇拜是纪律约束的一种. 事实上,这是所有纪律都来自的中心。 我们在公开学习其他基督徒时,学会私下崇拜耶稣. 在礼拜活动之前、期间和之后, 或许你可以带一个人到一个社区团体去唱歌、祈祷、相互承担负担, 或许你们都学到了新的款待方式。 也许你学会了如何更亲切和耐心的 分歧。 汝等学取欢喜相与相与相与相与相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相 你也可以带一个人一起来,当你的福音。 基督教徒通常不会传福音, 门徒们有没有机会 看看你如何和别人分享福音? 即使你做了这些事,你纪律严明的人 也必须能看到你和耶稣的行走, 以复制他们在日常生活中看到的。 门徒们不只看到耶稣在山上宣扬赛门教。 他们看到了中间的瞬间 他们不仅看到了他如何教书,还看到了他在教书后的所作所为. 耶稣确实说过:“因此,凡放松这些最最次要的诫命之一并教别人做同样的事情的人,在天国中称为最少的;凡这样做并教他们的人,在天国中称为伟大”(Matt. 5:19)。 分离为双重义务 将意味着带人 与你一起生活 最普通的时刻。 它既包括教学,也包括执行基督的命令。 在杂货跑。 绕行相邻. 你宁愿听音乐, 当你把其他的耶稣追随者带入你跟随耶稣的节奏时, 追随耶稣的所有生命都可以成为门徒他人的机会. 也许问题不应该是:我怎样才能让更多的时间给别人? 却取而代之:"我如何能用我的时间去门徒? 每个人都没有时间为每个人, 但每个人都有时间为某人。

articles.title: How God Used a Mafia-Man to Build His Church
articles.summary: Hannah Hagarty tells how God used an unexpected friendship with a deaf mafia leader to establish the first church in a remote city.
articles.summary_zh: 汉娜·哈加蒂（ Hannah Hagarty ）讲述了上帝如何利用与聋哑黑手党领导人的意外友谊，在一个偏远的城市建立了第一座教堂。
articles.title_zh: 神如何使用黑手党人建立他的教会
articles.content: Greg and Julie Dye moved halfway around the world to an unreached language group . They may have expected the hurdles of learning a new language and culture, but they could not have predicted how God would establish the first church among a people who had never heard of him. Eager to learn the local language, Greg and Julie diligently worked to establish connections and build friendships in the community. As Americans living in a city near the Mongolian border, they were impossible to miss. But none of the people they met were glad to see Americans. The Cold War had just ended. Tensions were tight. Their new area of the world had only recently opened to outsiders. Greg and Julie were followed, spit on, and they encountered persistent hostility. Greg was often picked up, interrogated, and then left in the woods to find his way back home. But one man noticed them and was glad to engage in conversation . Dava was deaf. Between his ability to speak and write a little, and Greg’s perseverance in the local language, a friendship began. Because the deaf people in the country spoke a language no one else could understand, the government had been suspicious of them. During the Cold War, they were gathered and sent by train to a remote city far away from the capitol. Signing in public became an illegal activity. As outcasts, they gathered scraps from the garbage to sell and worked the worst jobs available—anything to try to live. Greg and Julie knew none of this when they arrived in their new city, but God knew. He sent them to Dava. Dava was eager to teach his language. Greg and Julie, facing incredible opposition learning the local spoken language, began also to learn sign language. Dava was eager to know all about Greg and Julie. Every morning, he showed up at their little apartment, bounced their toddler around on his shoulders, and worked to teach them his language. When Greg had a break from the job that allowed them to stay in the country, he began the meticulous work of putting the gospel narrative that he’d come to share into sign language. When Dava heard about the upcoming story nights, he was excited and promised he’d bring some friends. AN UNEXPECTED TWIST On the first story night, Greg and Julie’s two-room apartment was packed full of deaf people. Those same people filled the tiny apartment every story week, month after month, to watch the telling of the gospel narrative. It was a story they had never been told, beginning at creation and the fall, then moving through the Old Testament . Each story left them wondering who would come to save God’s people. One night, in the sixth month, when the Redeemer had been revealed, Dava stood up, and his larger-than-life presence filled the room. “ Okay!” he bellowed. “I believe now.” He gestured to the two rooms of people and said, “You don’t have to keep coming if you don’t want to!” Greg and Julie watched the scene, not understanding what was happening. No one moved an inch. Dava turned to them. “I’m part of the deaf mafia,” he confessed. “I only made a friendship with you so that I could rob you. But now, I believe in Jesus.” He told Greg and Julie how, for the past six months, he’d threatened to hurt each individual present if they did not come to his American friend’s house once a week to listen to their stories. Knowing he was a murderer and wanted by the police, the deaf people in the apartment had taken his threats seriously. The moment Dava believed in Christ, he freed them from his threat. Now, 30 years later, Julie tells the rest of the story with joyful but tearful eyes: “ The thing is, they didn’t leave. Nearly all of them came back. They became the seed of the first church in that city, a deaf church, that God built as only he could do.” Shortly after his conversion, Dava turned himself in to the police. articles.content_zh: Greg和Julie Dye 在世界的半个角落 搬到了一个没有联系的语言组 他们可能已经预见到学习新语言和文化的障碍,但他们无法预料上帝会怎样在从未听说过他的民族中建立第一个教堂. 为了学习当地语言,格雷格和朱莉勤奋地努力在社区中建立联系并建立起友谊. 由于美国人住在蒙古边境附近的一城市,他们不可能错过. 但是他们遇见的人没有一个见到美国人就很高兴. 冷战刚刚结束。 紧张气氛很紧张。 他们的世界新地区最近才对外开放。 格雷格和朱莉被跟踪,吐口水,他们遭遇了持续的敌意. 格雷格经常被接走,审问,然后被留在树林中寻找回家的路. 但有一个人注意到他们,并很高兴参与对话。 达瓦是聋子。 在他说话和写作的能力与格雷格在当地语言的坚韧不拔之间,开始了友谊. 因为国内的聋人会说别人无法理解的语言,所以政府一直怀疑他们. 在冷战期间,他们被集合并被用火车送往远离卡皮托尔的偏远城市. 公开签名是一种非法活动。 作为被排斥者,他们从垃圾中收集出垃圾来出售并从事最坏的工作——任何试图活下来的工作。 格雷格和朱莉到达新城时并不知道这些,但上帝知道. 他把他们送到了达瓦。 达瓦热衷于教授他的语言. 格雷格和朱莉面对不可思议的反对派学习当地口语,也开始学习手语. 达瓦急于了解格雷格和朱莉的一切. 每天早上,他都出现在他们的小公寓里,在肩膀上弹起他们的幼儿,并努力教他们自己的语言. Greg中断了让他们留在国内的工作后, 当达瓦听到即将到来的故事之夜, 一个无法想象的TWIST 在第一个故事之夜,格雷格和朱莉的两间公寓被装满了聋人. 那些人每个故事周、每个月都填满小公寓,看福音故事的讲述。 这是他们从未听到的故事, 从创造和倒下开始, 然后通过旧约。 每个故事都让他们怀疑谁会来拯救真主的人民。 一天晚上,在6个月里,当救世主被揭发时,达瓦站起身来,他比生还长的身影填满了房间。 “好! ”他高呼“好! ” “我现在相信了。” 他向两个房间的人示好, Greg和Julie看了场景 不明白发生了什么 没有人动一英寸。 达瓦转向他们。 “我是聋人黑手党的一部分,”他承认。 “我只为了抢劫而与你建立了友谊。 但现在,我相信耶稣。” 他告诉格雷格和朱莉,在过去六个月里,他曾威胁说,如果他们每周不来美国朋友家听他们的故事,就会伤害在场的每一个人。 明知他是一个杀人犯并被警察通缉,公寓里的聋子们已经认真对待他的威胁. 达瓦一相信基督,就让他们摆脱了威胁. 现在,30年后,朱莉用欢快但泪眼讲述了剩下的故事:"事实是,他们没有离开. 他们几乎都回来了。 他们成为了该市第一个教堂 -- -- 一个聋子教堂 -- -- 的种子,这是上帝建造的,只有他才能做到。” 转会后不久,达瓦向警方自首. 他因犯罪入狱多年. Julie说:“这对他来说是件艰难的事,”但是他今天回到了教堂并活跃起来。 故事没有结束T

articles.summary_zh: 当大多数"南方浸信会"想到传教士时,他们常常会描绘出教会的植树人和福音派. 但国际使命委员会的领导人说,今天最需要的是那些在幕后工作的专业人员。 咨监委领导人报告说,教师、保健工作者、顾问、会计师、后勤专家和成员护理人员等关键角色正在帮助推进大委员会,许多教会从未看到过。 多琳·贝克,IMB导演
articles.title_zh: IMB寻求教师、医护人员、商业专业人士担任传教士
articles.content: IMB missionary Dr. Heidi Haun, left, checks on patients at Baptist Medical Centre in Nalerigu, Ghana. There are needed roles for IMB missionaries in healthcare, ministering to the needs of local populations and utilizing this time to minister to spiritual needs. IMB Photo When most Southern Baptists think of missionaries, they often picture church planters and evangelists. But leaders with the International Mission Board say some of the greatest needs today are for professionals whose work happens behind the scenes. IMB leaders report that critical roles such as teachers, healthcare workers, counselors, accountants, logistics specialists and member care personnel are helping advance the Great Commission in ways many churches never see. Doreen Baker, IMB director of TCK (third culture kid or missionary kid) education, sees a constant need for education professionals. Teachers are needed in international schools, which cover a variety of global educational entities, and in other settings to provide for missionary kids and their educational needs. “Teachers are significant in that not only are they providing instruction for students, but they are an integral part of the core missionary task ,” Baker said. “We also have great needs for consultants to support our families on the field with their children’s education in many ways.” Baker previously served 25 years teaching in Asia and experienced how education creates access to missions where traditional pathways may be limited. IMB missionary Ellie Bohrer teaches a 12th grade World Views class at Black Forest Academy in Germany. The IMB is seeking other educators, like Bohrer, who are willing to use their skills on the mission field. IMB Photo Scott Ray, IMB senior director of global deployment, noted that many missionary positions go unfilled simply because they fall outside traditional perceptions of missionary service. He said professional skills can provide both practical ministry support and access to countries where traditional missionary visas are difficult to obtain. Opportunities exist for finance professionals, veterinarians, medical workers, Send Relief personnel and others. Healthcare remains one of the most strategic areas in demand. Tom Hicks, IMB director of global health strategies, said many medical professionals have the wrong perception about mission work. “We do have an issue where people will select out because they don’t think that what they do is useful on the mission field,” he said. In reality, Hicks said many areas across the globe are increasingly seeking family medicine physicians, internists, pediatricians, pediatric nurse practitioners, OB providers, physical therapists, occupational therapists, speech pathologists and lactation consultants. The need is especially significant in sub-Saharan Africa, where young populations create a growing demand for pediatric care. Healthcare professionals also provide a unique advantage in countries that restrict missionary activity. “Missionaries with a vocational value, like healthcare missionaries, have opportunities to go places that others can’t go,” Hicks said. Another often-overlooked ministry is member care, which focuses on the spiritual, emotional, mental and relational health of IMB missionaries. Chris Martin is the IMB director of global member care. “Member care missionaries stand alongside those missionaries that are thought of traditionally as church planters or evangelists and support them,” Martin said. Many who serve in these roles come from counseling backgrounds and help missionaries navigate stress, conflict, grief and other challenges that can affect long-term ministry effectiveness. Martin compares their role to Aaron and Hur in Exodus 19, holding up Moses’ arms during battle, strengthening those serving on the front lines. articles.content: In South Asia, Maryam and a local pastor baptize Tara, a new believer. IMB missionaries work alongside local believers and churches to fulfill the Great Commission. IMB Photo Twenty minutes had passed already. The sun was going down, and they were looking everywhere, but they only saw men in the park. Sophia, an International Mission Board missionary, joined another IMB missionary and Maryam, a South Asian Christian. They went to the park to share the gospel, but approaching a man in their Muslim-majority city was out of the question. They kept walking and watching. Even if they went home without a single conversation, Sophia knew Maryam would want to try again. This woman who had grown up with a distrust of Muslims, now searched a park for a Muslim woman to tell about Jesus. When Sophia first invited her along, Maryam never imagined a Muslim could come to know Jesus. But the more they went out sharing the gospel together, the more God softened her heart. “One day, I found she was sharing in the park by herself, without me,” Sophia said with a laugh. These days, she shares regularly — with classmates, with rickshaw drivers, with women in the park, when she can find them. God transformed Maryam’s heart. He could transform this walk through the park, too. “So we stopped,” Sophia said, “and prayed, ‘God, give us just one woman to talk to.’” Then they spotted her — a girl sitting alone on a bench. Meeting the girl on the bench She looked like other conservative Muslim women in the area, covered in black except for her face. They approached casually, not wanting to frighten her. It was Eid al-Adha – “one of the biggest Muslim holidays here,” Sophia said. They greeted her and asked about her holiday plans. Her name was Tara, and she wasn’t intimidated at all. “You may think I’m a Muslim from the way I dress,” she said, “but actually in my heart, I have left Islam.” “I was a little shocked,” Sophia said, hearing such a bold statement from a stranger. Tara told them she was a university student at a conservative Islamic school, but she had grown disillusioned and discontent with the religion. “ I don’t believe in Islam anymore,” Tara said. Without knowledge of God, she had no one to pray to, and it left her lonely. She’d been searching — Buddhism and Hinduism from friends, even a meeting with atheists, who struck her as unhappy, following only themselves. “Do you know any Christians?” Sophia asked. “Would you like to hear what we believe?” “Sure, please share.” They read about Jesus’ birth, and Tara was hungry for more. When she asked about church, Sophia described their congregation of about 40 believers, many from a Muslim background. Though she wasn’t ready to visit the church, Tara continued her interest in learning. Sophia and Maryam met with her every week in coffee shops, tea shops, Sophia’s home, wherever they could talkthat wasn’t too loud or have “too many ears and eyes” observing them. Finding her closest friend They read through the Gospel of John. One November day in a coffee shop, they reached the passage on the Samaritan woman at the well, and Sophia noticed Tara was crying. “Tara, I see you have tears,” Sophia said. “Let’s stop. Let’s talk about it .” That day, Tara prayed to receive Christ. Soon after, she wanted to visit the church, though nervous how believers would receive her in a hijab. “They will love you,” Sophia told her. “Don’t worry.” Tara went and was welcomed. That Christmas, 80 people packed Sophia’s apartment, singing and dancing in circles. Across the room, Sophia saw Tara, wearing red Christmas garland like a scarf and a smile stretched across her face. “Tara grew up very conservative – music was not even allowed in her home. But now she’s dancing, worshiping the Lord with us with music and songs.” In South Asia, Maryam and a local pastor baptize Tara, a new believer. articles.content: The eastern face of St. Peter's Basilica in the Vatican City in Rome, Italy, is famous for its central balcony from which popes give their papal addresses. Most people in Rome have at least a cultural connection to Roman Catholicism as the city is “the heart of Catholicism.” IMB Photo In the city where Jason and Lizzy Davis serve, some steps have a lot of meaning. And the meaning is different for them than it is for the thousands who travel there to visit that site. “If you come to Rome, you can come to a place called the Holy Steps,” Jason said. “People go there, and they’ll crawl up on their knees and pray the rosary all the way up.” From the top of the steps, a mural depicting Jesus on the Cross looks down on those making the pilgrimage. For Jason and Lizzy, it’s a spiritual experience, a picture of a religion that asks people to earn their way to Jesus. “That’s really the opposite of what the gospel is. The gospel is Jesus saying, ‘No, you can’t do it . . . no matter how good you think you are,’” they said. Most people in Rome have at the very least a cultural connection to Roman Catholicism, as the city is “the heart of Catholicism.” Jason explained, “It’s where the Pope lives in the Vatican. It’s very much part of the religion and culture. It’s all intertwined here.” An ‘unavoidable’ call Jason and Lizzy are investing their lives as International Mission Board missionaries in Rome, Italy, to share the truth of the gospel. The Davises partner with national believers through a new church plant, and they’re seeking to plant more churches within the city. Lizzy said for her, the call to missions was unavoidable. “I grew up as a third culture kid, or a missionary kid. My parents were on the mission field, as were my grandparents, all with the International Mission Board.” Then her family moved to Virginia for her dad to work for IMB’s home office staff. As a middle schooler and high schooler, every time Lizzy heard about the need for the gospel to go forth, she felt a burden, a “burning” in her heart. She didn’t know what God would do with that, but she had a feeling she would see one day. Now, years later, she and Jason spend their time trying to find as many opportunities as they can to invite people into their home so they can share the hope of Jesus with them. That can mean Bible study or simply sharing a meal. ‘Completely lost’ Jason has been surprised by just how often people are willing to talk about faith. “You can get into spiritual conversations very quickly with people, especially if you’re just open and honest with them.” Lizzy shared that one of the easiest ways to do this is to be willing to let your day be interrupted. “That’s something I’ve seen Jason do firsthand in our neighborhood. He walks down the street, and everybody knows him because he stops and takes the time to ask them questions about their families, gets to know people, gets to know the newspaper stand guy and the guy at the fruit stand and the grocery store ladies.” She emphasized that caring about people is “what Christ would do.” The Davises, whose previous mission service prevents their photos from being published, live in a neighborhood of about 130,000 people. Their church of 15 people is the only evangelical congregation there. Lizzy said the area is “truly a lost, completely lost, dark neighborhood” with people who have never heard the gospel. articles.content: Rebeca Couto poses with her IMB teammates. Couto is a global missionary partner serving alongside IMB missionaries in Japan. IMB Photo Rebeca Couto poses with her violin. Couto is a professional violinist who is serving as a global missionary partner with the IMB in Japan. Doors have opened for her to use her skills with evangel ical Japanese musicians who perform. IMB Photo Rebeca Couto moved from one volcanic archipelago to another, leaving Portugal’s Azores islands to anchor her life in Japan. The percentage of evangelical Christians in the Azores and Japan is similar, with both populations under 1%. Couto is a fourth-generation Christian, a rarity on the small islands. She is one of few, if any, believers in the Azores with such a long spiritual lineage. This rich legacy shaped her and prepared her for ministry. “I’ve always understood the Great Commission as a call for all believers and all disciples of Christ to be missionaries, wherever they are, whatever they’re doing, and whatever God has equipped them with,” Couto said. Couto’s great-grandfather became a Christian through the witness of missionaries from the United Kingdom. Later, missionaries from the Foreign Mission Board, now the International Mission Board, started the first Baptist work in the Azores by planting an English-speaking church near an American military base. A Baptist Brazilian couple planted a Portuguese-speaking church, which became the congregation where Couto grew up and was commissioned as a missionary. Ministry has been passed down through the generations of her family. Couto’s father has pastored for 20 years, and both of her parents have been involved in ministry for most of their lives. articles.title_zh: IMB传教士使用家庭、咖啡馆、应用程序为西班牙的福音对话敞开大门
articles.content: Men and women gather to discuss spiritual topics with Caleb and Carina Beaty, International Mission Board missionaries who serve in Madrid. IMB Photo Across Spain, people looking for connection and meaningful conversation turn to the internet to find groups where they can meet others. At a café by the river, Caleb and Carina Beaty engage in conversations about finding purpose, beauty and “what’s wrong with the world.” A website called Meetup allows people to search for groups to meet in person. The description of the Beatys’ group indicates that it discusses spiritual topics. People come expecting to talk about faith, so it’s not a surprise when they arrive. Caleb said he always has a list of questions that begin broadly and funnel into questions such as, “If there were a God …” or “What do you think Christians believe about that?” or “Why do you think religions have such different perspectives?” The Beatys’ goal in these conversations is to work toward deeper worldview questions within 45 minutes to an hour. Most of the people who attend their Meetup group are from Madrid, but they also have conversations with people from other countries. During one Meetup, Caleb and Carina shared how creation was perfect, but sin led to a world separated from the Father. God offers salvation through the death and resurrection of Jesus, they explained. “There are times we’re able to get to a clear gospel presentation with a group of people, and sometimes we’re doing pre-evangelism.” Caleb said. Some repeat attendees who have been attending for more than a year quickly jump to the heart of the discussion. “All right, Caleb, what’s the Bible say about suffering?” they’ll ask. Caleb and Carina then have the opportunity to share the Christian perspective. IMB missionaries Caleb and Carina Beaty and their children pose for a photo in a park in Madrid, Spain.  IMB Photo Spain has secularized rapidly since the 1990s, Caleb said. While many may think of it as a Catholic nation, many people do not know the basic tenets of Christianity. “We’ve got all the churches, we’ve got the cathedrals, and they do processions, but the average person on the street does not know anything about the gospel and does not know anything about Jesus,” Caleb said. Younger Spaniards are drawn to their group and are receptive to the gospel because they don’t have a spiritual foundation or know anyone who does. “There’s just this curiosity because, for a lot of them, they’ve never met someone who actually believes that God exists, and that changes your life,” Carina said. “I’ve had people completely shocked that we believe in God. ‘You really believe that God exists?’ They can’t wrap their mind around that.” During one Meetup, a man contrasted Protestant and Catholic beliefs by saying Protestants focus on Jesus’ suffering and Catholics on Mary’s grief. Caleb responded that evangelicals focus on the resurrection. When Caleb said Jesus rose from the dead, the man replied that he needed to look into that. Caleb said encounters like that reveal how little many Spaniards know about the gospel. Caleb noted the irony of the man’s sharing the Catholic perspective without truly understanding it. He is not the only person the Beatys have met who has missed the heart of the gospel. A friend of the Beatys told them she’d heard Jesus died, but she hadn’t heard he rose from the dead. A man reads a passage of Scripture during a Bible study hosted by IMB missionaries Caleb and Carina Beaty at their family’s apartment in Madrid, Spain. Five atheists began attending their Bible study after attending the couple’s Meetup group. IMB Photo The Beatys also host seasonal outreach events through the Meetup. Members from their church in Madrid have started attending the Meetup to learn how the Beatys lead discussions. Their group has become so popular, a waitlist has formed. Caleb and Carina host a small-group Bible study in their home. Five atheists who joined their Meetup now attend the Bible study.

IMB Photo The chapel at Council Road Baptist Church in Oklahoma City turned into a science lab on Oct. 5-6. Microscopes, beakers and test tubes weren’t in the room, but this Sending Church Lab drew nearly 40 people representing 12 Oklahoma Baptist churches committed to send and care for international missionaries well. The Sending Church Lab, facilitated by the International Mission Board, brought pastors, church leaders and missionaries together for two days of discussion, self-assessment and planning centered on one question: What does it mean for a church to truly be a sending church?
